list.name: board
list.query: SELECT name AS __text, id AS __value FROM boards WHERE id LIKE 'linear:%' ORDER BY name
list.label: Issue board

list.name: contributor
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '(unattributed)') AS __text, COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '') AS __value FROM whodunit_repos ORDER BY 1
list.label: Contributor

options.content:
## GenAI Adoption — Executive Summary
*How much of this team's delivery is AI-assisted, and what it costs or saves.* Every number below is measured from git history and the agent's own session records — none of it is self-reported or estimated.

panels.title: AI-assisted commits

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) v FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id WHERE c.status='assisted' AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.description:
Commits carrying evidence of agent involvement in the selected range.

Counts `status = 'assisted'` only. A commit with no trailer is `undetermined` — no evidence either way — not proof it was written without an agent (NAV-21). Read this against Attribution coverage beside it, which is the share of commits that carry any verdict at all.

panels.title: Attribution coverage

targets.rawSql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(c.status<>'undetermined')/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0),0) v FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.description:
Share of commits carrying any attribution verdict — anything other than `undetermined`.

This is a measure of **instrumentation, not of AI use**. A repository instrumented last week has low coverage for its whole history, because commits made before the hooks existed cannot be attributed retroactively.

Low coverage means the numbers on this page describe a small slice. Read every other panel against it.

panels.title: Code acceptance

targets.rawSql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(e.outcome='accepted')/NULLIF(SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')),0),1) v FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.description:
Share of decided tool calls that were accepted.

**The denominator is decided calls only** — accepted, rejected or failed — not all calls. A call whose outcome was never recorded is excluded rather than counted as accepted, which would flatter the rate. See Decided tool calls beside this for the size of that denominator.

A rejection is a human declining; a failure is the tool erroring. Both count as decided, and only acceptance is in the numerator.

panels.title: Decided tool calls

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) v FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed') AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.description:
How many tool calls have a recorded outcome, and therefore how much the acceptance rate beside this is actually measured on.

Shown because a percentage without its denominator is not a measurement. A rate over a handful of calls moves entirely on one of them.

panels.title: Agent sessions

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e.session) v FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE e.session<>'' AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.description:
Distinct agent sessions that produced at least one recorded event in range.

A session is one conversation with an agent. Sessions that only read or ran commands count here — this measures how often an agent was used, not how much code resulted.

options.content:
### Does AI-assisted work ship faster?
Cycle time for issues whose commits carry an AI-attribution trailer, against those that don't. **A measured comparison, not an estimate** — if the *Not AI-assisted* count is zero there is no control group yet and the delta means nothing. That count is shown deliberately.

panels.title: Median cycle — AI-assisted

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(ltm)/60,1) v FROM (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) t WHERE ai=1

panels.description: Issues whose commits carry an attribution trailer, against those that do not. Read it as a description, not a verdict: harder work tends to get handed to an agent, so a longer AI-assisted cycle usually reflects which issues were chosen, not the agent slowing them down.

panels.title: Median cycle — not AI-assisted

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(ltm)/60,1) v FROM (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) t WHERE ai=0

panels.description: Issues whose commits carry an attribution trailer, against those that do not. Read it as a description, not a verdict: harder work tends to get handed to an agent, so a longer AI-assisted cycle usually reflects which issues were chosen, not the agent slowing them down.

panels.title: Issues compared (AI)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(*) v FROM (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) t WHERE ai=1

panels.description:
Tracker issues resolved in range whose linked commits include assisted work.

The denominator behind the cycle-time comparison. An issue counts as AI-assisted when **any** commit on it was assisted, so a mostly-manual issue with one assisted commit lands here.

Requires a connected issue tracker in DevLake. Empty means no issues were linked, not that no AI work happened.

panels.title: Issues compared (non-AI)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(*) v FROM (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) t WHERE ai=0

panels.description:
Tracker issues resolved in range with no assisted commits linked.

The other half of the cycle-time comparison's denominator. Both counts are shown because a difference in medians means nothing without them — and these two groups are **not** matched work: an agent is reached for on some kinds of issue and not others.

panels.title: Delta

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(
   (SELECT AVG(ltm) FROM (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) a WHERE ai=0)
 - (SELECT AVG(ltm) FROM (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) b WHERE ai=1), 0) / 60 v

panels.description: Issues whose commits carry an attribution trailer, against those that do not. Read it as a description, not a verdict: harder work tends to get handed to an agent, so a longer AI-assisted cycle usually reflects which issues were chosen, not the agent slowing them down.

panels.title: Cycle time by issue

targets.rawSql:
SELECT issue_key AS `Issue`,
       CASE ai WHEN 1 THEN 'AI-assisted' ELSE 'not AI-assisted' END AS `Attribution`,
       ROUND(ltm/60, 1) AS `Cycle hours`,
       resolution_date AS `Resolved`
FROM (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) t
ORDER BY resolution_date DESC

panels.description:
Every compared issue with its cycle time, so the medians above can be checked against the rows that produced them.

Cycle time is DevLake's `lead_time_minutes`, rendered in hours. Attribution is per issue: assisted when any linked commit was.

Listed rather than summarised because with this few issues a median is one or two rows moving.

options.content:
### Trend
Use the **Granularity** control above to switch between daily, weekly and monthly buckets.

panels.title: AI-assisted commits over time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       SUM(c.status='assisted') AS `assisted`,
       SUM(c.status='undetermined') AS `undetermined`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id
WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description:
Assisted against undetermined commits per day.

The undetermined series is **not** a 'no AI' series — it is commits carrying no evidence either way, which includes everything before instrumentation. A rising assisted line against a falling undetermined one usually means coverage improving, not adoption rising.

panels.title: Agent edits & lines written over time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       COUNT(*) AS `agent edits`,
       SUM(e.lines_added) AS `lines added`
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id
WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description:
Recorded agent edits per day, and the lines those edits added.

Edits count tool calls that touched a file; lines count what those calls wrote. The two diverge when the agent makes many small changes or a few large ones, which is the shape worth noticing.

Lines from rejected or failed calls are excluded — text that never reached a file is not authored code.

panels.title: Acceptance rate over time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(e.outcome='accepted')
             /NULLIF(SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')),0),1) AS `accept %`
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id
WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description:
Daily acceptance rate over decided tool calls.

Same denominator rule as the headline figure: only calls with a recorded outcome. A day with few decided calls swings violently, so read the shape over weeks rather than the value on any one day.

panels.title: Issues resolved over time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(i.resolution_date) AS `time`,
       SUM(t.ai = 1) AS `AI-assisted`,
       SUM(t.ai = 0) AS `not AI-assisted`
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
  AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) t ON t.issue_key = i.issue_key
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board' AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description:
Issues resolved per day, split by whether any linked commit was assisted.

Requires a connected issue tracker. The split is per issue rather than per commit, so an issue with one assisted commit among ten counts as assisted.

options.content:
### Where the AI is being applied
Purpose is classified from the commit itself, not self-reported.

panels.title: AI-assisted work by purpose

targets.rawSql:
SELECT c.purpose AS `metric`, COUNT(*) AS `value`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id
WHERE c.status='assisted' AND c.purpose<>'' AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
  AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY c.purpose ORDER BY `value` DESC

panels.description:
What kind of work the agent was used for, from Conventional Commit prefixes and path heuristics.

**Purpose is a label, not an observation.** `feature` is reachable only through a literal `feat:` prefix, so a repository not using Conventional Commits will show almost none — which says nothing about the work itself.

panels.title: Acceptance by tool

targets.rawSql:
SELECT e.tool AS `Tool`,
       SUM(e.outcome='accepted') AS `Accepted`,
       SUM(e.outcome='rejected') AS `Rejected`,
       SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')) AS `Decided`,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(e.outcome='accepted')
             /NULLIF(SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')),0),1) AS `Accept %`
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id
WHERE e.tool<>'' AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY e.tool ORDER BY `Decided` DESC

panels.description:
Acceptance broken down by which tool the agent used, with the decided count beside each rate.

The counts matter more than the percentages here: a tool used three times shows 0% or 100% and neither means anything. Sorted by decided volume so the rates worth reading are at the top.

panels.title: Session engagement

targets.rawSql:
SELECT LEFT(s.session,8) AS `Session`,
       ROUND((s.last_seen-s.first_seen)/60000000000) AS `Minutes`,
       s.user_messages AS `Prompts`,
       s.tool_calls AS `Tool calls`,
       s.distinct_tools AS `Tools`
FROM whodunit_sessions s JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=s.repo_id
WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
ORDER BY s.first_seen DESC

panels.description:
Individual sessions with their duration, prompt count and tool activity — the raw shape behind the aggregates above.

Prompts count user messages only, excluding the harness replying to the agent with tool results. Minutes are first to last recorded event, so a session left open overnight reads as long without being busy; read it against tool calls.

panels.title: Commits — assisted vs the rest

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       SUM(c.status = 'assisted') AS `assisted`,
       SUM(c.status <> 'assisted') AS `not assisted`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id
WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')
  AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description: Stacked, so the bar height is total commit volume and the blue share is adoption. A flat blue band before instrumentation is expected — those commits predate whodunit and are not evidence that no agent was used.

panels.title: Issues opened vs completed

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(i.created_date) AS `time`,
       COUNT(*) AS `opened`,
       SUM(i.status = 'DONE') AS `completed`
FROM issues i JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.created_date IS NOT NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(i.created_date)
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description: Both series are keyed on the date an issue was opened, so 'completed' is how many of that week's issues are now done — not how many were closed that week. Recent weeks therefore look worse than they will.
